statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, when a UAC sends a request to a proxy server, the proxy server MAY authenticate the originator before the request is processed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy MUST populate the 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) message with a Proxy-Authenticate header field value applicable to the proxy for the requested resource.
actions: populate 407 response with Proxy-Authenticate header field value

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Proxies MUST NOT add values to the Proxy-Authorization header field.
actions: do not add values to Proxy-Authorization header field

statements.subject: server
statements.description: All 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) responses MUST be forwarded upstream toward the UAC following the procedures for any other response.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When the originating UAC receives the 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) it SHOULD, if it is able, re-originate the request with the proper credentials.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If no credentials for a realm can be located, UACs MAY attempt to retry the request with a username of "anonymous" and no password (a password of "").
actions: retry request with username='anonymous' and password=''

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The UAC SHOULD also cache the credentials used in the re-originated request.
actions: cache credentials used in re-originated request

statements.subject: sip
statements.description: The following rule is RECOMMENDED for proxy credential caching:

statements.subject: client
statements.description: These credentials MUST NOT be cached across dialogs; however, if a UA is configured with the realm of its local outbound proxy, when one exists, then the UA MAY cache credentials for that realm across dialogs.
actions: do not cache credentials across dialogs

statements.subject: client
statements.description: These credentials MUST NOT be cached across dialogs; however, if a UA is configured with the realm of its local outbound proxy, when one exists, then the UA MAY cache credentials for that realm across dialogs.
actions: cache credentials for outbound proxy realm across dialogs

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any UA that wishes to authenticate itself to a proxy server -- usually, but not necessarily, after receiving a 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response -- MAY do so by including a Proxy-Authorization header field value with the request.
actions: include Proxy-Authorization header field value in request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When multiple proxies are used in a chain, a Proxy-Authorization header field value MUST NOT be consumed by any proxy whose realm does not match the "realm" parameter specified in that value.
actions: do not consume Proxy-Authorization header field value

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Note that if an authentication scheme that does not support realms is used in the Proxy-Authorization header field, a proxy server MUST attempt to parse all Proxy-Authorization header field values to determine whether one of them has what the proxy server considers to be valid credentials.
actions: parse all Proxy-Authorization header field values to identify valid credentials

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Because this is potentially very time-consuming in large networks, proxy servers SHOULD use an authentication scheme that supports realms in the Proxy-Authorization header field.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each WWW-Authenticate and Proxy-Authenticate value received in responses to the forked request MUST be placed into the single response that is sent by the forking proxy to the UA; the ordering of these header field values is not significant.
actions: aggregate all WWW-Authenticate and Proxy-Authenticate values into single response sent to UA

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When resubmitting its request in response to a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) that contains multiple challenges, a UAC MAY include an Authorization value for each WWW-Authenticate value and a Proxy-Authorization value for each Proxy-Authenticate value for which the UAC wishes to supply a credential.
actions: include Authorization value for each WWW-Authenticate challenge
include Proxy-Authorization value for each Proxy-Authenticate challenge

statements.subject: message
statements.description: As noted above, multiple credentials in a request SHOULD be differentiated by the "realm" parameter.
actions: differentiate multiple credentials by realm parameter

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When it retries a request, a UAC MAY therefore supply multiple credentials in Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header fields with the same "realm" parameter value.
actions: supply multiple credentials with same realm parameter value in Authorization or Proxy-Authorization headers

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The same credentials SHOULD be used for the same realm.
actions: use same credentials for same realm
